correctness.rationale: PASS: Affine normalization sets John ellipse to B² and transforms genuine centrally symmetric six-tangent polygons into three opposite normal pairs. The symmetric John criterion is 0<θ_i≤π/2 and Σθ_i=π; contact vectors doubled in angle have origin in their convex hull. Direct shoelace/support-line computations give |K|=2Σtan(θ_i/2) and |K°|=Σsin θ_i. The resulting separable S=2Σf(θ_i), f=tan(t/2)+sin(t)/2, extends continuously to a compact cap triangle. On the boundary θ1=π/2, θ2+θ3=π/2; tangent-addition and AM-GM show the maximum only at θ2=θ3=π/4, giving S=5√2−1. Interior constrained equal-first-derivative cases have either equal angles (S=7√3/2) or golden-ratio two-equal saddle with positive second derivative direction; neither exceeds the boundary. Equality representative K0 is square clipped on two opposite diagonal corners, area 4√2−2 and polar 1+√2. Florian (1995), main theorem, gives S≥6 and square-only equality; genuine hexagons cannot attain but a continuous admissible degenerating hexagon path realizes all intermediate S values. Taylor expansion at maximizing gaps gives positive linear coefficient 3√2/2−2 in η and quadratic coefficient 8−11√2/2 in δ² with the stated mixed remainder. Source symbolic verifier matches normal area formulas but universal conclusion rests on exact optimization, not numeric sampling.
